outcome.answer: Yes—some papers report that geometry-motivated optimizers outperform Adam on challenging non-convex tasks, though the evidence is specific to the tested settings. ArcGD outperformed Adam on the highly non-convex Rosenbrock benchmark under one learning-rate comparison and achieved better final solutions in most cases under another [1]. EISAM also reports higher test accuracy and training efficiency than Adam across benchmark datasets, using loss-landscape geometry to guide updates [6]. In other domains, Muon improves over Adam on equivariant architectures [2], and matrix-structured optimizers can improve convergence and final accuracy for interatomic potentials [4]. These results do not establish that geometry-based methods generally beat Adam on all non-convex surfaces.
